answer: Tidal Bridge Pricing: each identity must hold a balance across two separate coordination pools and move value between them on a fixed schedule. A bridge of matched transfers is only credited when both sides clear within the same tide window; unmatched legs wait and decay. Sybil attackers must fund and synchronize every fake identity across both pools, so each additional identity doubles the capital tied up and the failed-crossing loss they absorb, making N identities cost roughly N times the single-identity coordination burden rather than one shared river of capital.
